\subsection{System under test}
\label{sec:methods-system}

SemPointer chunks context into blocks of at most $B=512$ tokens with the reader tokenizer
(\texttt{experiments/sempointer/pipeline.py::chunk\_text}), merging a trailing fragment shorter
than $B/8$ into the previous block [ESTABLISHED]. Each block gets one $k=8$ pointer and resolves
to $m=1$ block per query in all final runs [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{config\_table.json}: $k=8$,
$m=1$, \texttt{rag\_m} $=1$, \texttt{block\_size} $=512$). Resolution uses $M_{\mathrm{text}}$: the
selected block's verbatim text enters the prompt (\texttt{prompt\_builder.py::build\_sempointer\_prompt}) [ESTABLISHED].

\paragraph{Selection disclosure.}
\label{sec:methods-selection}
Selection is dense cosine similarity between a mean-pooled query embedding and mean-pooled
per-block pointer embeddings (\texttt{experiments/sempointer/scorer.py::PointerScorer.score\_all})
with the public \texttt{sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2} encoder [ESTABLISHED]. Blocks past
the encoder's maximum length are embedded in full: \texttt{embed\_long} (\texttt{pointer\_generator.py})
splits text into \texttt{max\_seq\_length} windows and mean-pools them, so a 512-token block is
represented whole, not truncated [ESTABLISHED]. Pointer identifiers (\texttt{[PTR\_id: ...]}) are
prompt-resident strings only for unselected blocks, carrying no key--value state: substrate point M1
(text) [ESTABLISHED]. The discrete address (seeded random-projection buckets, space $V_p^k$) comes from
\texttt{SemanticIDPointerGenerator} [ESTABLISHED]; scoring uses the dense block embedding from the same
encoder object, so dense RAG sees identical representations [ESTABLISHED].

\subsection{Scope: text substrate only}
\label{sec:methods-scope}

All measured claims concern $M_{\mathrm{text}}$. Key--value ($M_{\mathrm{kv}}$) and latent ($M_{\mathrm{latent}}$)
substrates are future work only: no KV-cache reuse, cross-block attention repair, or learned
compression in any reported run [ESTABLISHED]. The KV-compress pilot (Table~\ref{tab:N4-kv-pilot}) runs
KVPress methods as black-box baselines at $n=10$, not a SemPointer KV substrate [ESTABLISHED].

\subsection{Cost model: prefill versus decode}
\label{sec:methods-cost}

We report two cost quantities; Eq.~7 covers only the first. \textit{Per-request prefill} is the one-time
forward cost of ingesting the active prompt; it scales with prompt length and dominates total latency
for long contexts here [REASONED]. \textit{Per-token decode} is the incremental cost per generated token,
$O(Ld)$ per step in length $L$ and width $d$ for cached decoding [ESTABLISHED textbook]. Sparse methods
shrink only the prefill term; nothing here claims a decode-complexity improvement [REASONED]. Reported
latency is end-to-end wall clock (prefill plus decode) from \texttt{GenResult.latency\_ms}, with token counts
from the real tokenizer (\texttt{experiments/engine/llm.py}) [ESTABLISHED]; per-call peak VRAM uses
\texttt{torch.cuda} counters reset before each call [ESTABLISHED].

\subsection{Additional baseline systems (implemented, pilot pending)}
\label{sec:methods-newbaselines}

Four further systems in \texttt{experiments/baselines/} share the uniform \texttt{System} interface but were
\textit{not} in the final runs and carry no numbers here [ESTABLISHED]: (i)~\texttt{agentic\_pointer.py}: the
LM itself routes among \texttt{[PTR\_id: preview]} strings (two calls per question, routed blocks capped at
$m=4$) [ESTABLISHED]; (ii)~\texttt{iterative\_rag.py}: two-round retrieve--draft--retrieve on the expanded
query, answering from the union of both rounds (two calls) [ESTABLISHED]; (iii)~\texttt{hybrid.py}:
reciprocal-rank fusion of BM25 and dense-cosine ranks ($\mathrm{rrf\_k}=60$), top-$m$ via the shared path
[ESTABLISHED]; (iv)~\texttt{session\_summary.py}: incremental per-block session summaries (one summarizer call
per block, cached) plus a top-1 BM25 raw block [ESTABLISHED]. Evaluation is pending; they are stated to
complete the design space.

\subsection{Benchmark protocols and adaptations}
\label{sec:methods-benchmarks}

All suites run on one reader (\texttt{Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct}, NF4, greedy, seed~42) on a single 8\,GB GPU
with CPU-only embedding fallback; no other GPU inference [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{BENCHMARK\_PROVENANCE.md} \S4,
\texttt{stats.json}: \texttt{seed} $=42$). RAG baselines retrieve $m=1$ block with the same MiniLM encoder
and \texttt{embed\_long} full-block representation [ESTABLISHED].

\paragraph{RULER (synthetic).}
\label{sec:methods-ruler}
Examples come from a faithful re-implementation of the official generators (\texttt{benchmarks/ruler.py}:
templates, task arguments, haystack sizing, needle depths), scored by the official per-sample containment
rule ($1.0$ if the reference string appears, else $0.0$) [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{BENCHMARK\_PROVENANCE.md} \S1).
Deviations: 5-essay cache (not 275), vendored word lists, approximate word-based haystack sizing, flat
\texttt{max-new-tokens} of~32, and chunked-block prompts with the project system prompt instead of the official
one [ESTABLISHED]. Final run: $n=180$ per system [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{stats.json}).

\paragraph{LongBench (real-document QA).}
\label{sec:methods-longbench}
Six tasks (\texttt{hotpotqa} \cite{yang2018hotpotqa}, \texttt{2wikimqa}, \texttt{musique} \cite{trivedi2022musique}, \texttt{multifieldqa\_en}, \texttt{narrativeqa} \cite{kovcisky2018narrativeqa},
\texttt{qasper}) from official \texttt{data.zip} on the byte-identical loading path, full test splits
($200/200/200/150/200/200 = 1150$), scored by verbatim official normalization plus Counter-based token F1
maximized over ground truths [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{BENCHMARK\_PROVENANCE.md} \S2). Deviations: flat
\texttt{max-new-tokens} of~64 (official per-task maxima 32/32/32/64/128/128) and chunked-block ingestion with
the project system prompt [ESTABLISHED]. Scored $n$: 1150 (SemPointer, RAG, BM25); 1136 for full context after
14 narrativeqa OOMs (see \S\ref{sec:results-oom}) [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{stats.json}).

\paragraph{LoCoMo (conversational memory).}
\label{sec:methods-locomo}
Ten official conversations from \texttt{locomo10.json} (sessions numerically ordered, turns in file order;
category~5 golds as \texttt{not mentioned}) [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{BENCHMARK\_PROVENANCE.md} \S3). Metric adaptation
(stated on every LoCoMo table): the official GPT-4 judge plus Porter-stemmed F1 is unavailable, so \textit{all}
categories use plain token F1 without stemming [ESTABLISHED]. Every result reads ``LoCoMo (token-F1 adaptation)''
and is not comparable to published LoCoMo numbers [ESTABLISHED]. Final run: $n=199$ per system [ESTABLISHED].

\subsection{Statistical methods}
\label{sec:methods-stats}

Comparisons use example-identifier-matched rows only [ESTABLISHED]
(\texttt{stats.json}: \texttt{n\_scored\_pairs\_note}). Binary containment (RULER, kv pilot) uses the exact
McNemar test on discordant pairs (correct $== 1.0$); continuous F1 (LongBench, LoCoMo) uses Wilcoxon
signed-rank [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{stats.json} \texttt{mcnemar\_note} fields). Effects report paired Cohen's
$d_z$ plus pooled $d$ [ESTABLISHED]. Intervals are paired bootstrap 95\% CIs (10\,000 resamples, seed~42)
[ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{stats.json}: \texttt{n\_bootstrap} $=10000$). The 13 primary paired tests use Bonferroni
$\alpha = 0.05/13 \approx 0.0038$ [ESTABLISHED] (\texttt{stats.json}: \texttt{bonferroni}).

\subsection{ConfigurationLedger}
\label{sec:methods-config}

True mean LLM tokens per block $B$ is $506.6$ (RULER), $504.2$ (LongBench), $510.2$ (LoCoMo), and $487.9$
(kv pilot); with $k=8$, $\kappa = k/B_{\mathrm{true}}$ is $0.0158$, $0.0159$, $0.0157$, $0.0164$ [ESTABLISHED]
(\texttt{config\_table.json}). Mean blocks per example (SemPointer rows): $24.75$ (RULER), $26.67$ (LongBench),
$28.0$ (LoCoMo), $7.5$ (kv pilot) [ESTABLISHED]. Recomputed score means match \texttt{metrics.json} on every suite
(\texttt{match}: true) [ESTABLISHED].
